sprint: Three voice-note badges, and none of them is a solid backfill. The product owner's own words: "i like the voice icon, but its overpowering with backfill can you allow creator to choose from 3 different voice note icons." The glyph was never the problem — the fixed coral disc behind it was.
task: A voice note's payload is audio, so the badge IS the only thing a silent surface can show, and its look is the one thing a kid can genuinely style. Ship 2 drew one fixed solid coral disc; three looks now replace it, catalogued once in js/stickerLibrary.js's VOICE_ICONS (value/label/glyph) with getVoiceIcon falling back rather than throwing on an unknown value. speaker — the glyph alone on a soft white halo, legible over a dark photo with no disc behind it, and the default; bubble — the glyph inside a drawn speech bubble with a tail, thin coral outline over a 14% tint; mic — a microphone glyph inside a thin coral ring, nothing inside it. renderer/slideRenderer.js's _drawSceneVoice dispatches on the look and the Object Strip card follows the chosen glyph, so a fourth look would be one catalogue entry plus one draw branch. The picker sits in the Refine panel's voice group beside Play — where the kind's own controls already live — reusing the shared .icon-row/.icon-card vocabulary, with only the preview swatch voice-specific so each tile SHOWS the look it picks. An absent voiceIcon resolves to speaker, which means an already-placed note picks up the lighter default rather than keeping the heavy disc: a deliberate, disclosed appearance change, since the heavy disc is exactly what was reported. Verified 20/20 first run via voice_icon_verify: the catalogue and its fallback, three cards labelled Speaker/Bubble/Mic with the default active on a note that stores no voiceIcon yet, and a coral-pixel census over the badge's own box — 0% for speaker (no backfill at all), ~10% for bubble and ~11% for mic (a real outline, not a fill), where the old solid disc would have been most of the box — plus each pick persisting, the Object Strip glyph following to the mic, and all three looks hashing to genuinely different pixels. Screenshotted all three side by side on a dark backdrop rather than trusting the numbers. Regression: voice_note 22/22 (one assertion updated — it sampled a single pixel expecting the solid coral disc this ship removes, now checks the badge box carries real ink), voice_place 16/16, voice 16/16, combined_widget 27/27, spatial_controls 40/40, four_bugs 36/36, image_studio_draw 26/26, Museum Gallery's three canonical hashes byte-identical (1f54eb660f7beb53 / 843e68f2cffb3c2e / 969a67e5c984647b), both goldenBuilds PASS.
